notes: FROZEN -- no phases. codex 0.153.0 DOES have a blocking dialog that names no tool call: a server-driven MCP elicitation. Its client side is generic and shipped-on-by-default (rmcp-client/src/elicitation_client_service.rs handles elicitation/create and openai/elicitation/create as an ordinary server REQUEST, not inside a tool-call future; codex-mcp/src/elicitation.rs raises EventMsg::ElicitationRequest and does not auto-approve under AskForApproval::UnlessTrusted; tui/src/bottom_pane/mcp_server_elicitation.rs blocks on it; features/src/lib.rs marks tool_call_mcp_elicitation and auth_elicitation Stage::Stable, default_enabled: true). The other three triggers the row lists do not qualify on codex. The sandbox/network-access confirmation exists (ApprovalAction::NetworkAccess, "Do you want to approve network access to ...") but carries the exec `command`/`cwd`/`hook_command` because it is raised from an exec that is already running -- a tool-carried episode, so it belongs to tool-gate-permission-prompt / permission-gate-non-mutating-tool. The two first-use trust prompts (tui/src/cwd_prompt.rs workspace trust, tui/src/startup_hooks_review.rs hook trust) are startup gates raised before the thread takes a turn, so there is no working->waiting edge, only a delayed birth; the driver's boot gates answer both. And codex has no auto-mode/settings-review dialog at all -- the nearest, "Would you like to grant these permissions?", is raised by the built-in request_permissions TOOL (core/src/tools/handlers/request_permissions.rs), and AskForApproval::Granular{sandbox_approval, rules, skill_approval, request_permissions, mcp_elicitations} is configuration, not a prompt. NONE OF IT IS OBSERVABLE, which is why this cell carries no phases. irrlicht has exactly two channels into a codex session and a tool-free dialog reaches neither. No hook: every PermissionRequest codex can fire comes from run_permission_request_hooks (core/src/hook_runtime.rs:246), whose only caller is core/src/tools/approvals.rs, and all seven ApprovalAction variants (ExecCommand, WriteStdin, Execve, ApplyPatch, McpToolCall, NetworkAccess, RequestPermissions) are carried by a tool call; codex's hook event set (PreToolUse|PermissionRequest|PostToolUse|PreCompact|PostCompact|SessionStart|SessionEnd|UserPromptSubmit|SubagentStart|SubagentStop|Stop|Interrupt) contains no Notification and no elicitation event, so unlike claudecode there is no matcher irrlicht could widen, and the legacy `notify` program carries a single variant, AgentTurnComplete (hooks/src/legacy_notify.rs). No transcript trace: rollout/src/policy.rs files EventMsg::ElicitationRequest -- with ExecApprovalRequest, ApplyPatchApprovalRequest, RequestPermissions and RequestUserInput -- under `// Transient, non-durable events.`, so it is never written to the rollout JSONL the FilesUnderRoot Source tails. Both edges the row asserts are therefore missing, and the trailing idle has nothing to catch: the session reads working (or ready, if the rollout tail already looks turn-done) for the whole time the modal blocks. That is no-trace-exists, i.e. incapable, not bug. VACUOUS-PASS WARNING for whoever revisits this: on codex a recording of this row cannot tell 'the dialog never painted' from 'the dialog painted and the daemon saw nothing' -- both yield an events.jsonl with no waiting episode. Any waiting a codex recording DID show here would by construction come from something else (the rollout turn-done / waiting-cue path, or a stray tool approval). Never grade this row without independent proof the modal was on screen, e.g. a tmux pane capture carrying the elicitation text. RE-ASSESS WHEN any of: codex routes elicitations through ApprovalAction (irrlicht's codex PermissionRequest matcher is already ".*", so it would receive them with no change on our side); codex gains a hook event for interactions/elicitations; codex moves EventMsg::ElicitationRequest out of the non-durable list so the rollout carries it (then this becomes an ordinary parser change and the arc the claudecode and antigravity siblings already state applies verbatim); or the adapter gains a Source over the app-server protocol stream. The contrast case is the recorded 2-19 cell: a TOOL-carried codex overlay is equally absent from the rollout, and reaches waiting only because the hook makes up for it -- this row has no hook to make up for it.
